title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Groups and Blocks
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Elements in the **s-block** and **p-block** (excluding the noble gases) are collectively known as:
questions.explain: The elements in Groups 1, 2, and 13–18 (s and p blocks) are often called representative or main-group elements because their outer shells are being filled.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which general electronic configuration represents the **d-block** elements (Transition Metals)?
questions.explain: Transition metals are characterized by the filling of inner d-orbitals. The general configuration is $(n-1)d^{1-10} ns^{0-2}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: An element has the atomic number 35. To which block and group does it belong?
questions.explain: Atomic number 35 corresponds to Bromine ($Br$). Its configuration ends in $4s^2 3d^{10} 4p^5$. Since the last electron enters a p-orbital, it is in the p-block. With 7 valence electrons ($s^2 p^5$), it belongs to Group 17 (Halogens).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following sets of atomic numbers belongs to the **Alkali Metals** (Group 1)?
questions.explain: Group 1 elements are Li (3), Na (11), K (19), Rb (37), etc. Option (b) is Alkaline Earth Metals, (c) is Halogens, and (d) is Noble Gases.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The metalloids (semi-metals) are located along a 'staircase' line on the periodic table. Which of the following elements is a **metalloid**?
questions.explain: Silicon ($Si$) is a classic metalloid, exhibiting properties intermediate between metals and nonmetals. Aluminum is a metal; Phosphorus and Sulfur are nonmetals.
questions.subject: Chemistry
